misp-threat-actor.description: WageMole is a North Korean state-sponsored APT that employs social engineering and technology to secure remote job opportunities in Western countries, leveraging stolen personal data from the Contagious Interview campaign. Threat actors create fake identities, including passports and driver's licenses, and prepare study guides for interviews, often utilizing generative AI for well-structured responses. They target small to mid-sized businesses and utilize job platforms like Upwork and Indeed, while employing automation scripts for account creation. WageMole's activities include sharing code within their group and requesting payments through platforms like PayPal to conceal their identity.

misp-tidal-groups.description:
Famous Chollima is a North Korea-linked threat group known for using job-themed social engineering campaigns ("Contagious Interview") to entice targets into downloading cross-platform malware, for example under the pretext of coding assignments or fixing browser issues during video assessments. The group has been observed setting up front companies as part of its schemes.<sup>[[The Hacker News Contagious Interview April 25 2025](/references/68d9fec5-40b0-414a-9d39-21b5f36a013b)]</sup> The group has also been linked to schemes facilitating the fraudulent hiring of remote North Korean IT workers by Western firms in an effort to evade sanctions.<sup>[[Unit 42 November 21 2023](/references/930228c3-a93b-4664-ab7d-65af212211fc)]</sup>

Security researchers have described Famous Chollima as being motivated by both espionage goals (stealing sensitive information) and financial ones (theft of cryptocurrency from software professionals).<sup>[[The Hacker News Contagious Interview April 25 2025](/references/68d9fec5-40b0-414a-9d39-21b5f36a013b)]</sup><sup>[[TrendMicro Void Dokkaebi April 23 2025](/references/8677d97f-6bca-48b8-9e0b-2bbcafae25e9)]</sup> Reserachers have described Famous Chollima as a "subgroup" of the North Korean state-sponsored Lazarus Group.<sup>[[Silent Push Contagious Interview April 24 2025](/references/7062304e-91e9-45bf-84b4-c42bdad99e23)]</sup>

limitations: Exact normalized-name matching does not prove one-to-one actor identity.
MISP Galaxy is an aggregation layer; original references remain authoritative.
A no-match result means no exact match in the fixed datasets, not that the actor does not exist.
A Malpedia name match confirms catalogue presence only, not actor use.
